after: Prior to your first session, read through the induction and the full return in waking life, so you’re more familiar with them. Give yourself a chunk of time when you can be physically secure for the time it takes. Then put the screen away. You’re learning to run the practice yourself, so don’t keep reading along like it’s a checklist.

And all this inner work has to lead somewhere. You should come out of it kinder to people, or humbler, or making better decisions, or doing real service, or with an everyday life that works better than before.

When I hypnotize myself, though, my dialogue with the system itself is immediate, and that's an advantage nobody outside my own head can duplicate. I found that especially amplified with loveyhuasca. My experiences included a much deeper understanding of my motivations, peaceful loving awareness operating alongside analytical clarity, the disappearance of unhelpful daydreaming, different priorities around relationships, stronger intuition, and repeated correction between intuition, subconscious response, and conscious analysis.

For people starting from there, I came up with something I call “borrowed adulthood.” I think of it as a provisional bridge, and I pieced it together from familiar practices like modeling and supported action. I’m not saying the whole sequence has been formally tested and proven as one treatment, though.

Keep it simple. Stick to the one thing you're doing, with one anchor or image to get started and one way to come back. You can also set yourself a tone if you want one, maybe warm or bounded or directed or neutral witnessing, or whatever else. If you're going to use metaphors just do one, and if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that's conscious.

Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional. You can use whatever form of signal shows up (feelings, rhythms, movements, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, lack of signal, whatever) but if you're using words, try to keep them related to whatever world you're creating. If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world. And when you're done, come back the other way. (It's fine to borrow qualities like warmth or steadiness. Just don't change who you are.)

In fractionation, you come back up toward ordinary awareness. Then you decide whether to go into absorption again. If you use fractionation openly, it teaches you that you can come out of trance as well as go in. At some point in time you can add this, but you must say you are doing it before doing it, so no answer can secretly mean “deeper.”

You could say something like 'What are you protecting me from?' or 'Are you afraid I will lie to myself again?' or 'Are you afraid this will just be a performance?' If it says yes, that one can sting, because there could be something to it. Maybe you've fooled yourself before, and that part of you remembers it. "Tell me what you remember, I'm listening." works well here.

Once you get an answer, you can ask: “What can I do in my ordinary life to prove that I heard correctly?” If it tells you to do something, I'd only do it if it's loving and leaves you free. It would have to make sense too. And even with all that, I wouldn't do anything big or hard to undo until I'm calm and I've checked it against what I actually know.
You use the prompt to tell your subconscious what you want. The NLP in Appendix B can make getting it safer. Even so, that doesn’t mean whatever answer you get is automatically true.

With an embedded invitation, you tuck a small direction into a longer sentence, and you shouldn't be hiding a demand in it. The direction should invite a modest shift inside you. ie. "And I can allow myself to experience..."
A Manipulative Double Bind Question is rigged so that you wind up doing what the speaker wants, whatever answer you give.

Reframes are dishonest when they make the problem into something that was good all along. Instead, ask yourself questions like What else might be true? or What is this part trying to do for me? or How might my Nurturer reframe this? or How might my Protector reframe this? or How might my Guide reframe this? etc., etc.
I won’t tell anyone to override their fear without first asking what it’s protecting.

Work with the body. Sometimes the mind is too activated for meditation to help, so you may need to work directly with the body to calm it down. Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc. (Avoid massaging the front of the neck. Also avoid massaging injured or numb body parts, or bruised, inflamed, or recently surgically operated on areas, or varicose veins. Also stop if the massage makes the anxiety symptoms worse, or makes you feel bad in any way, such as painful, dizzy, tingly, etc.) You’ve got lots of other options for the body too, like heat, pressure, a weighted blanket, darkness, your favorite calming music, or a massage gun if you’re careful with it, etc. Use whatever actually helps you, and don’t go surrounding the anxiety with a heap of wellness stuff.

Here is some inner child love. Put your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexus, and say to yourself in a loving way, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t need to fix it. I’m here now. The adult is here right now to listen to you.” When you say this, really talk to your inner child, who’s scared to death. If you don’t feel any warmth today, there’s no need to fake it. Just rest your hands there and notice what you find.

A lot of people have OPENED themselves up to love at one point in their life. If you've had a similar experience, know that there is a difference between having experienced it at one point, or only being able to access it in a certain state, and being able to get to it at any point in your life. While you're building a way to reach love on a normal day, let that experience show you what can happen. (If you can't give that love to the child, try to deal with why you can't, instead of trying to ramp up the experience. Often it’s a protective part that’s seen love come with strings before. Hear it out first.)

You don’t have to find out if it’s a guard immediately, and you may not be able to comfort it quickly. Just keep an eye on whether the way you’re responding to it helps you get clearer and steadier and less hooked.

For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask one clear question and wait, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous signal: write down what you get, whether that's a word, a sensation, an impulse, an objection, or silence, and don't take it as proof. Deepener: none. Doing the inner contact fully alert doesn't make it a lesser version. Handoff: have your adult self answer the question however makes sense, ideally by writing something or doing something. Integration/exit: reality test the signal, then act on it in one small way. You didn't go into trance, so just close the exercise and get on with your day.
